1.g3 g6 2.Bg2.strategy: Completes the fianchetto: the bishop on the long diagonal presses on b7 and on the centre from a distance. White keeps the pawn set-up flexible, but leaves Black free to claim the centre first.

1.g3 g6 2.c4.strategy: Claims queenside space and controls d5, reaching an English Opening with an early g3. The pawn occupies no central square, so Black develops naturally and claims a share of the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.Nf3.strategy: Develops the knight, guarding d4 and e5, and leaves the pawn set-up undecided. Black develops freely and can take central space before White has chosen.

1.g3 g6 2.b3.strategy: Prepares Bb2 to contest the long diagonal, but 2...Bg7 hits the rook on a1 through the empty b2 square, and 3.Bb2 Bxb2 loses a piece, since nothing guards b2. White must first block the diagonal, so the double fianchetto costs an extra move and loosens the queenside.

1.g3 g6 2.c3.strategy: Prepares d4 with pawn support and blocks the long diagonal in advance of ...Bg7. It develops no piece and takes c3 from the queen's knight, while Black develops freely and takes the centre. The move is sound but passive.

1.g3 g6 2.d3.strategy: Supports a later e4, opens the c1-bishop and prepares a compact set-up with a kingside fianchetto, Nf3 and castling. It is sound but slow, since it takes no central space and lets Black develop and claim the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.d4.strategy: Takes the centre at once and reaches the same position as opening with 1.d4 and playing g3 second. It is sound but gives up the flexibility of 1.g3, and Black hits the centre at once.

1.g3 g6 2.e3.strategy: Prepares a compact kingside set-up while keeping d4 available. It is solid but slow: the e3-pawn shuts in the c1-bishop, and Black develops freely and takes the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.e4.strategy: Occupies the centre at once and reaches the same position as opening with 1.e4 and playing g3 second. Bg2 then backs the pawn along the long diagonal, and a compact set-up with d3, Nf3 and castling follows. Nothing guards e4 yet, so Black can strike at it with ...d5, when 3.exd5 Qxd5 hits the rook on h1, or build calmly.

1.g3 g6 2.f4.strategy: Takes control of e5 and prepares to develop the kingside with a fianchetto and castling. The pawn weakens e4 and opens the g1-a7 diagonal before the king is safe, so Black develops and aims at the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.Nc3.strategy: Develops the queen's knight and covers d5 and e4, aiming for a kingside set-up with a fianchetto. The knight blocks the c-pawn, so c4 has to wait, and Black can develop and take the centre. The move is sound, but it commits the knight before White has chosen a pawn set-up.

1.g3 g6 2.a3.strategy: Spends a tempo on a rim pawn to prepare b4 and does nothing for the centre or development. Black develops and takes space in the centre while White has yet to develop a piece.

1.g3 g6 2.a4.strategy: Gains queenside space and takes b5 from Black, but loosens b4 and the b3 square and leaves the centre untouched. Black develops and builds in the centre at leisure.

1.g3 g6 2.b4.strategy: Grabs queenside space but leaves b2 empty, so 2...Bg7 attacks the rook on a1 at once and 3.Bb2 Bxb2 loses a piece. White must spend a move blocking the diagonal, and the b4-pawn becomes a target for ...a5.

1.g3 g6 2.f3.strategy: Blocks the long diagonal of the bishop meant for g2 and takes f3 from the king's knight. It also opens the g1-a7 diagonal towards White's king and does nothing for the centre, so Black develops and takes the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.h3.strategy: Takes g4 from Black's bishop and knight but spends a tempo on a rim pawn that adds nothing to White's position. Black develops and takes the centre first.

1.g3 g6 2.h4.strategy: Prepares h5 against the g6-pawn, but Black can stop it with ...h5 or simply develop and take the centre. The advance leaves the g3-pawn guarded only by f2 and develops nothing.

1.g3 g6 2.Na3.strategy: Develops the knight to the rim, where it eyes b5 and c4 but blocks the a-pawn and guards nothing in the centre. Black takes the centre with ...d5, which also covers c4, and develops freely while the knight needs more moves to find a post.

1.g3 g6 2.Bh3.strategy: Puts the bishop on h3, where it attacks only the guarded d7-pawn, instead of on the long diagonal. After ...d5 the c8-bishop opposes it, so the bishops come off or White spends another move returning to the long diagonal, while Black develops.

1.g3 g6 2.Nh3.strategy: Heads for f4 or g5, but the knight stands on the rim, away from the centre, instead of on f3. Black develops and takes the centre, and ...e5 also takes f4 from the knight.

1.g3 g6 2.g4.strategy: Moves the g-pawn a second time, loosens the kingside for good and leaves the pawn on g4 unguarded. After ...d5 or ...d6 the c8-bishop attacks it, as does ...h5, and White must spend further moves just to keep it.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 Bg7.strategy: Completes the fianchetto: the bishop looks down the long diagonal at c3 and b2, and Black mirrors White's set-up. Neither side has a pawn in the centre yet, so the game stays flexible and whoever commits first shows their plan.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 Nf6.strategy: Develops the knight to its natural square, where it covers d5 and e4. Black keeps every set-up open, and the centre stays unoccupied for both sides.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 d5.strategy: Takes the centre at once and gains space, but the bishop on g2 already bears on d5, so Black has to keep the pawn supported.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 c5.strategy: Fights for d4 and gains queenside space, the mirror of White's own set-up. The cost is a centre left to White: if d4 is met by ...cxd4, Qxd4 hits the h8-rook along the open long diagonal until Black blocks it.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 e5.strategy: Takes a share of the centre at once, with the kingside fianchetto behind it. The pawn is committed before any piece is out: Nf3 attacks it immediately, and after d4 exd4 Qxd4 the queen hits the h8-rook along the open diagonal.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 Nc6.strategy: Develops the knight, eyes d4 and e5 and blocks the long diagonal of Bg2 at c6. The knight takes the square of the c-pawn, though, so ...c5 and ...c6 are off the table, and White can take space in the centre before Black has chosen a structure.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 d6.strategy: Frees the c8-bishop and heads for a Modern or King's Indian set-up. The centre is left to White for now, who can take space with the bishop on g2 already developed.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 c6.strategy: Prepares ...d5 with a pawn behind it and blocks the long diagonal of Bg2 at c6, so a later ...b6 or ...b5 no longer drops the a8-rook. The centre is left to White for now, and the c-pawn is committed before the centre has taken shape.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 e6.strategy: Prepares ...d5 in a compact set-up. The e6-pawn shuts in the c8-bishop, which can come out only via d7 or, after ...b6, via b7, and ...b6 must wait until ...d5 or ...c6 has closed the long diagonal.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 f5.strategy: Takes control of e4 and builds the pawn structure of the Leningrad Dutch. The set-up is double-edged: it loosens e6 and the king's cover, and White can develop freely.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 Na6.strategy: Puts the knight on the rim, where it eyes b4 and c5 but covers no central square. White uses the time to develop and take the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 Nh6.strategy: Sends the knight via the rim towards f5, where a pawn on e4 would chase it away; from h6 it covers no central square. White simply develops and takes the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 Bh6.strategy: Puts the bishop on h6 instead of g7, where the d2-pawn stops it and it takes no part in the fight for the long diagonal. Once d3 or d4 opens the c1-h6 diagonal, Black must either allow the trade of dark-squared bishops, leaving the squares weakened by ...g6 without their defender, or spend another move on ...Bg7.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 a6.strategy: Spends a tempo on a rim pawn that prepares ...b5, but that advance would drop the a8-rook to Bxa8 as long as the long diagonal stays open. White just develops and takes the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 a5.strategy: Gains queenside space and takes b4 from White's pieces, but develops nothing. White can develop and take the centre with a free hand.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 f6.strategy: Prepares ...e5, but blocks the long diagonal in front of the future g7-bishop, takes f6 from the king's knight and opens the a2-g8 diagonal towards the king's castling square. White develops while Black has nothing out.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 h6.strategy: Spends a tempo on a rim pawn that only takes g5 from White's pieces and brings Black no closer to developing. White just develops and takes the centre.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 h5.strategy: Gains kingside space and prepares ...h4 to attack g3, but develops nothing. White can stop the advance at once with h4.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 g5.strategy: Moves the g-pawn a second time and leaves it unguarded on g5: once d3 or d4 opens the c1-bishop, Bxg5 is threatened, and Black must spend another move defending it. The kingside stays loosened for good.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 b6.strategy: Hangs the rook: with the b-pawn gone from b7, the long diagonal is open to a8, and 3.Bxa8 takes the rook, since neither the c8-bishop nor the queen can recapture. Even if the bishop is later trapped in the corner, White stays at least an exchange up.

1.g3 g6 2.Bg2 b5.strategy: Opens the long diagonal to a8: 3.Bxa8 takes the rook, and no black piece can recapture there. White stays at least an exchange up even if the bishop is later trapped, and the queenside space is no compensation.
